hook.text: Two buildings, 500 meters apart. Running fiber costs thousands. A wireless bridge costs hundreds.

buildup.text: Outdoor bridges use directional antennas to create a point-to-point link between locations through air.

discovery.text: Modern bridges hit gigabit speeds over several kilometers using protocols optimized for outdoor use.

twist.text: Line of sight is required. Trees, buildings, or heavy rain can block or degrade the signal.

climax.text: Ubiquiti's airMAX and Cambium's ePMP have connected schools, farms, and villages worldwide.

punchline.text: Wireless bridges link buildings without digging. Cheap and fast.

quiz.question: What is required for an outdoor wireless bridge to work?
options: Clear line of sight between the two antennas
A fiber optic cable between the buildings
Both buildings must use the same ISP

details.summary: Outdoor wireless bridges create network links between buildings using focused radio beams, often spanning distances of several kilometers.
details.whyItMatters: Wireless bridges provide a cost-effective alternative to running fiber between buildings. They are essential for connecting remote sites, campus buildings, and temporary installations.
takeaways: Point-to-point bridges connect two locations with focused beams
Distances of several kilometers are achievable with clear line of sight
Throughput can exceed 1 Gbps with modern millimeter-wave equipment

faq.question: What range can outdoor wireless bridges achieve?
faq.answer: Standard 5 GHz bridges reliably cover 5 to 10 kilometers with clear line of sight. High-gain directional equipment can reach 20 kilometers or more. Millimeter-wave bridges in the 60 GHz band offer multi-gigabit speeds but are limited to about 1 to 2 kilometers.

faq.question: Do wireless bridges require line of sight?
faq.answer: Optimal performance requires clear line of sight between both antennas with no obstructions in the Fresnel zone. Trees, buildings, and terrain can degrade or block signals. Mounting antennas on towers or rooftops and performing a site survey ensures reliable connectivity.
